mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the pattern reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the effect reverses during periods of strong wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the pattern fails during periods of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month indicates a disinflationary tightening regime, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered months, or the pattern reverses during periods of strong credit expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a precautionary savings behavior that foreshadows lower future demand and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises AND GDPC1 falls > -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 55% of triggered months, or the effect disappears during periods of fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 4% combined with a simultaneous decline in average hourly earnings (not directly observed but implied by labor market weakness) over two months signals deteriorating wage pressure, which reduces consumer purchasing power and corporate pricing power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the pattern reverses during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 1 million units for four consecutive months signals a housing market contraction, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on broader GDP growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of rapid mortgage rate declines.
